essence: Posterize quantizes continuous image color values into a limited number of discrete tonal steps. Lowering Level reduces the available steps, forcing neighboring tones to share the same value and creating visible bands; raising it restores smoother tonal transitions. Effect Opacity mixes the quantized result back with the original image.
manifests_as: Smooth gradients and subtle shading break into flat, stepped color regions, producing a graphic poster-print or low-bit-depth appearance.

key_levers.name: Level
key_levers.effect: Lower values force more pixels into the same few tonal bins, making larger and harsher bands; higher values retain more tonal separation and look progressively closer to the source.

key_levers.name: Effect Opacity
key_levers.effect: Controls the mix of the posterized output over the original: 100 shows full quantization, while lower values retain original smooth shading beneath the stepped result.

enums_to_verify.GPU Rendering (ADBE Force CPU GPU, 1-3): Unverified: likely selects a CPU/GPU rendering or compatibility mode. Its value-to-label mapping is unknown and it should not be assumed to change the intended posterization look.

reasoning_hooks: Level is the primary look control: it changes tonal quantization, not saturation, hue selection, or a fixed palette.
At Level 255 the effect may be nearly invisible on normal footage because most tonal precision is retained.
Effect Opacity does not create finer posterization; it only blends the already-quantized image with the untouched source.
Effects are evaluated in stack order: blur, glow, grain, or other smoothing applied after Posterize can soften or obscure its bands; placing Posterize after those effects quantizes their output too.
Posterization reads most clearly on gradients, soft lighting, skin shading, skies, and other areas with continuous tonal transitions.
